rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second “Have you considered?” repeats the first occurrence.
rows.anchor: { أرأيت إن كان على الهدى * أو أمر بالتقوى } أرأيت تكرير للأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional is the second object of Have you considered; its answer is omitted and supplied by the answer to the second conditional, which serves as its counterpart.
rows.anchor: والشرطية مفعوله الثاني ، وجواب الشرط محذوف دل عليه جواب الشرط الثاني الواقع موقع القسيم له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks about the one forbidding a servant’s prayer: is the forbidding man guided or enjoining piety as he believes in idol worship, or denying truth and turning from right? God sees each one’s guidance and error.
rows.anchor: أو آمرا بالتقوى فيما يأمر به من عبادة الأوثان كما يعتقده ، أو إن كان على التكذيب للحق والتولي عن الصواب كما تقول

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation contrasts a praying servant who is guided and enjoining piety with a forbidding man who denies truth and turns away, and marvels at the situation.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المعنى أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا يصلي ، والمنهي على الهدى آمرا بالتقوى ، والناهي مكذب متول ، فما أعجب من ذا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the second address speak to the unbeliever, as a judge addresses two litigants in turn: would he forbid prayer that guides and calls to God?
rows.anchor: وقيل : الخطاب في الثانية مع الكافر ، فإنه سبحانه وتعالى كالحاكم الذي حضره الخصمان : يخاطب هذا مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Piety is mentioned in the rebuke but not the prohibition because the prohibition concerned prayer and the command to piety; prayer alone suffices as an active call.
rows.anchor: ولعله ذكر الأمر بالتقوى في التعجب والتوبيخ ، ولم يتعرض له في النهي ؛ لأن النهي كان عن الصلاة والأمر بالتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, forbidding a praying servant may concern prayer or other matters; people’s states are encompassed by perfecting oneself through worship and others through calling them.
rows.anchor: أو لأن نهي العبد إذا صلى يحتمل أن يكون لها ولغيرها وعامة أحوالها محصورة في تكميل نفسه بالعبادة وغيره بالدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional is the second object of Have you considered; its answer is omitted and supplied by the answer to the second conditional, which serves as its counterpart.
rows.anchor: والشرطية مفعوله الثاني ، وجواب الشرط محذوف دل عليه جواب الشرط الثاني الواقع موقع القسيم له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks about the one forbidding a servant’s prayer: is the forbidding man guided or enjoining piety as he believes in idol worship, or denying truth and turning from right? God sees each one’s guidance and error.
rows.anchor: أو آمرا بالتقوى فيما يأمر به من عبادة الأوثان كما يعتقده ، أو إن كان على التكذيب للحق والتولي عن الصواب كما تقول

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation contrasts a praying servant who is guided and enjoining piety with a forbidding man who denies truth and turns away, and marvels at the situation.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المعنى أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا يصلي ، والمنهي على الهدى آمرا بالتقوى ، والناهي مكذب متول ، فما أعجب من ذا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the second address speak to the unbeliever, as a judge addresses two litigants in turn: would he forbid prayer that guides and calls to God?
rows.anchor: وقيل : الخطاب في الثانية مع الكافر ، فإنه سبحانه وتعالى كالحاكم الذي حضره الخصمان : يخاطب هذا مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Piety is mentioned in the rebuke but not the prohibition because the prohibition concerned prayer and the command to piety; prayer alone suffices as an active call.
rows.anchor: ولعله ذكر الأمر بالتقوى في التعجب والتوبيخ ، ولم يتعرض له في النهي ؛ لأن النهي كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, forbidding a praying servant may concern prayer or other matters; people’s states are encompassed by perfecting oneself through worship and others through calling them.
rows.anchor: أو لأن نهي العبد إذا صلى يحتمل أن يكون لها ولغيرها وعامة أحوالها محصورة في تكميل نفسه بالعبادة وغيره بالدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rebukes the forbidding man; the threat applies if he does not stop what he is doing.
rows.anchor: { كلا } ردع للناهي { لئن لم ينته } عما هو فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat means God will seize him by the forelock and drag him by it into the Fire.
rows.anchor: { لنسفعنا بالناصية } لنأخذن بناصيته ولنسحبنه بها إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safʿ means grasping something and pulling it forcefully.
rows.anchor: والسفع القبض على الشيء وجذبه بشدة

rows.speaker: قرئ
rows.claim: The verb is also read with a doubled nūn, or as la-asfaʿanna.
rows.anchor: وقرئ لنسفعن بنون مشددة ؛ ولأسفعن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The muṣḥaf writes the form with an alif according to the convention of pausal spelling.
rows.anchor: وكتابته في المصحف بالألف على حكم الوقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase omits a possessive suffix because the lām suffices and the intended forelock is understood to belong to the person mentioned.
rows.anchor: والاكتفاء باللام عن الإضافة للعلم بأن المراد ناصية المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is an apposition to the preceding forelock; the apposition is permitted because it is qualified.
rows.anchor: { ناصية كاذبة خاطئة } بدل من الناصية ، وإنما جاز لوصفها

rows.speaker: قرئ
rows.claim: It is also read in the nominative, understood as ‘it is a forelock,’ or in the accusative as a form of blame.
rows.anchor: وقرئت بالرفع على هي ناصية ، والنصب على الذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the forelock lying and erring ascribes its owner’s qualities to it metaphorically for emphasis.
rows.anchor: ووصفها بالكذب والخطأ وهما لصاحبها على الإسناد المجازي للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is told to call the people of his assembly so they can help him.
rows.anchor: { فليدع نادية } أي أهل ناديه ليعينوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nādī is the council or gathering place where people sit together.
rows.anchor: وهو المجلس الذي ينتدي فيه القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Abu Jahl passed the Prophet while he prayed, claimed he had more supporters in the valley, and the verse came down about summoning the guards to drag him to the Fire.
rows.anchor: روي أنا أبا جهل لعنه الله مر برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصلي فقال : ألم أنهك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The summoned zabāniya are to drag the threatened man into the Fire.
rows.anchor: { سندع الزبانية } ليجروه إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zabāniya are guards; their singular is zabniyya, like ʿifrīya, from pushing, or zabnī by relation, with tāʾ replacing the original yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وهو في الأصل الشرط ، واحدها زبنية كعفرية من الزبن وهو الدفع ، أو زبني على النسب وأصلها زباني والتاء معوضة عن الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā again rebukes the forbidding man; the Prophet should stay obedient, continue prostrating, and draw near to his Lord.
rows.anchor: { كلا } ردع أيضا للناهي { لا تطعه } أي اثبت أنت على طاعتك { واسجد } داوم على سجودك { واقترب } وتقرب إلى ربك

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A hadith says a servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating; Bayḍāwī gives no grading or named transmitter.
rows.anchor: أقرب ما يكون العبد إلى ربه إذا سجد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet promises the reward of reciting the whole Mufaṣṣal to whoever recites Sūrat al-ʿAlaq; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصل كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kanūd means ungrateful for blessings, disobedient in the language of Kinda, or stingy in the language of Banū Mālik.
rows.anchor: { إن الإنسان لربه لكنود } لكفور ، من كند النعمة كنودا ، أو العاص بلغة كندة ، أو لبخيل بلغة بني مالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement is the answer to the oath.
rows.anchor: أو لبخيل بلغة بني مالك ، وهو جواب القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-khayr here means wealth, as in the verse saying ‘if he leaves wealth’ (2:180).
rows.anchor: المال من قوله سبحانه وتعالى { إن ترك خيرا } أي مالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shadīd means stingy, or intensely attached to wealth.
rows.anchor: { لشديد } لبخيل ، أو لقوي مبالغ فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible object of the oath is the afternoon prayer, because of its excellence.
rows.anchor: أقسم سبحانه بصلاة العصر لفضلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible object of the oath is the age of Prophethood.
rows.anchor: أقسم سبحانه بصلاة العصر لفضلها ، أو بعصر النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further sense is time, which contains wondrous events.
rows.anchor: أو بالدهر لاشتماله على الأعاجيب ، والتعريض بنفي ما يضاف إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath indirectly denies that loss is attributable to time.
rows.anchor: والتعريض بنفي ما يضاف إليه من الخسران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People lose in their endeavors and in spending their lifetimes pursuing their aims.
rows.anchor: إن الناس لفي خسران في مساعيهم ، وصرف أعمارهم في مطالبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article is generic, while the indefinite form magnifies the loss.
rows.anchor: والتعريف للجنس ، والتنكير للتعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who do righteous deeds trade the world for the afterlife and win eternal life and everlasting happiness.
rows.anchor: فإنهم اشتروا الآخرة بالدنيا ، ففازوا بالحياة الأبدية ، والسعادة السرمدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truth is what cannot rightly be denied, in belief or action.
rows.anchor: الثابت الذي لا يصح إنكاره من اعتقاد أو عمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience means abstaining from sins, steadfastness on truth, or enduring what God tests His servants with.
rows.anchor: عن المعاصي ، أو على الحق ، أو ما يبلو الله به عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning truth and patience coordinates specific qualities with the general category for emphasis, unless deeds are restricted to acts that perfect the individual alone.
rows.anchor: وهذا من عطف الخاص على العام للمبالغة ، إلا أن يخص العمل بما يكون مقصورا على كماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He mentions the cause of profit without spelling out loss, to state the aim, imply other paths bring loss or a diminished share, and graciously leave loss implicit.
rows.anchor: بأن ما عد إما عد يؤدي إلى خسر ونقص حظ ، أو تكرما ، فإن الإبهام في جانب الخسر كرم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says reciting Sūrat al-ʿAṣr earns forgiveness and places the reciter among those who counsel one another in truth and patience; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم :  " من قرأ سورة ( والعصر ) غفر الله له ، وكان ممن تواصوا بالحق وتواصوا بالصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra’s Meccan or Medinan classification is disputed; it has seven verses.
rows.anchor: سورة الماعون مختلف فيها ، وآيها سبع آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arāʾayta is an interrogative used to express amazement.
rows.anchor: { أرأيت } استفهام معناه التعجب ، وقرئ

rows.speaker: قرئ
rows.claim: It is read arayta without hamza, assimilated to the imperfect; the interrogative opening may ease that form, and another reading adds kāf.
rows.anchor: وقرئ ( أريت ) بلا همزة إلحاقا بالمضارع ، ولعل تصديرها بحرف الاستفهام سهل أمرها ، و( أرأيتك ) بزيادة الكاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dīn may mean recompense or Islam.
rows.anchor: الذي يكذب بالدين بالجزاء أو الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhī may be generic or refer to a known individual; the following verse supports the definite, known-person reading.
rows.anchor: و( الذي ) يحتمل الجنس والعهد ، ويؤيد الثاني قوله{ فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaduʿʿ means to shove the orphan away violently.
rows.anchor: يدفعه دفعا عنيفا ، وهو أبو جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One identification is Abu Jahl, guardian to an orphan who came unclothed seeking his own property and was shoved away.
rows.anchor: وهو أبو جهل ، كان وصيا ليتيم فجاءه عريانا يسأله من مال نفسه فدفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account identifies Abu Sufyan: after he slaughtered a camel, an orphan asked for meat and he struck the child with his stick.
rows.anchor: أو أبو سفيان نحر جزورا فسأله يتيم لحما فقرعه بعصاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other identifications are al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra or a miserly hypocrite.
rows.anchor: فقرعه بعصاه ، أو الوليد بن المغيرة ، أو منافق بخيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view takes the figure as a miserly hypocrite in general.
rows.anchor: أو الوليد بن المغيرة ، أو منافق بخيل

rows.speaker: قرئ
rows.claim: An alternative reading yadʿ means to leave the orphan.
rows.anchor: أو منافق بخيل . وقرئ ( يدع ) أي يترك

none: Verse text only; no commentary is included in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are heedless of their prayer and do not care about it.
rows.anchor: أي غافلون غير مبالين بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They display their deeds to people so that people will praise them.
rows.anchor: يرون الناس أعمالهم ليروهم الثناء عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-māʿūn means the alms tax, or items customarily lent from one person to another.
rows.anchor: الزكاة أو ما يتعاور في العادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ introduces the consequence clause.
rows.anchor: والفاء جزائية ، والمعنى إذا كان عدم المبالاة باليتيم من ضعف الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If disregard for the orphan shows weak religion, heedlessness of prayer, ostentation, and withholding zakāt deserve woe even more; prayer is religion’s pillar, ostentation a branch of unbelief, and zakāt its bridge.
rows.anchor: فالسهو عن الصلاة التي هي عماد الدين ، والرياء الذي هو شعبة من الكفر ، ومنع الزكاة التي هي قنطرة الإسلام ، أحق بذلك ، ولذلك رتب عليها الويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the fāʾ is causal, meaning ‘so woe to them.’
rows.anchor: أو للسببية على معنى فويل لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them worshippers rather than using a pronoun highlights their bad treatment of both Creator and creatures.
rows.anchor: وإنما وضع المصلين موضع الضمير للدلالة على سوء معاملتهم مع الخالق والخلق

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet promises forgiveness to whoever recites Sūrat Araʾayta if he pays zakāt; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : " من قرأ سورة ( أرأيت ) غفر له إن كان للزكاة مؤديا "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Masad is Meccan and has five verses.
rows.anchor: سورة المسد مكية ، وأيها خمس آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabbat means perished or lost; tabāb is loss that leads to destruction.
rows.anchor: { تبت } هلكت أو خسرت ، والتباب خسران يؤدي إلى الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two hands stand for Abu Lahab himself, as in the expression about not throwing oneself into destruction by one’s hands.
rows.anchor: { يدا أبي لهب } نفسه ، كقوله تعالى { ولا تلقوا بأيديكم إلى التهلكة }

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says the two hands mean Abu Lahab’s worldly life and afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد بهما دنياه وأخراه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An occasion report says that after the command to warn his nearest kin, the Prophet gathered and warned them; Abu Lahab cursed him, objected to the summons, and seized a stone to throw, so the sūra was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنما خصتا ؛ لأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لما نزل عليه { وأنذر عشيرتك الأقربين } جمع أقاربه فأنذرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is called by his honorific kunya because it was how he was famous.
rows.anchor: وإنما كناه ، والتكنية تكرمة لاشتهاره بكنيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kunya avoids naming him ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, a name the author says was disliked.
rows.anchor: وإنما كناه ، والتكنية تكرمة لاشتهاره بكنيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kunya may fit his fate among the people of the Fire.
rows.anchor: ولأنه لما كان من أصحاب النار كانت الكنية أوفق بحاله ، أو ليجانس قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible reason for the kunya is its sound match with the later phrase dhāt lahab.
rows.anchor: أو ليجانس قوله { ذات لهب }

rows.speaker: قرئ
rows.claim: It is also read Abū Lahab with nominative Abū, as in the expression ʿAlī ibn Abū Ṭālib.
rows.anchor: وقرئ ( أبو لهب ) كما قيل :( علي بن أبو طالب )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second clause reports after a prayer, and the past tense conveys that the destruction is certain to occur.
rows.anchor: وتب } إخبار بعد دعاء ، والتعبير بالماضي لتحقق وقوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites an unnamed poetic line, especially qad faʿala, as an analogue for a past expression that makes an outcome certain.
rows.anchor: كقوله : جزاني جزاه الله شر جزائه جزاء الكلاب العاويات وقد فعل

rows.speaker: قرئ
rows.claim: Another reading adds qad: wa-qad tabb.
rows.anchor: ويدل عليه أنه قرئ ( وقد تب )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the first clause reports what his hands earned and the second reports his own deed.
rows.anchor: أو الأول إخبار عما كسبت يداه ، والثاني عن عمل نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause either denies that his wealth benefited him when destruction came, or rhetorically asks in denial whether it benefited him.
rows.anchor: نفي لإغناء المال عنه حين نزل به التباب ، أو استفهام إنكار له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the interrogative reading, mā is in the accusative position.
rows.anchor: أو استفهام إنكار له ، ومحلها النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā kasab may mean his earnings or acquisitions through wealth, such as offspring, profits, prestige, and followers.
rows.anchor: وكسبه أو مكسوبه بماله من النتائج والأرباح والوجاهة والاتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may instead mean deeds he thought would benefit him.
rows.anchor: أو عمله الذي ظن أنه ينفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another identification is his son ʿUtba, whom a lion mauled on the road to Syria.
rows.anchor: أو ولده عتبة وقد افترسه أسد في طريق الشام

words: مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُۥ وَمَا كَسَبَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab died of al-ʿadasa a few days after Badr, was left three days until decomposed, and was finally buried by hired Sudanese; the account treats this as fulfilled prediction.
rows.anchor: مات أبو لهب بالعدسة بعد وقعة بدر بأيام معدودة ، وترك ثلاثا حتى أنتن ، ثم استأجروا بعض السودان حتى دفنوه

words: مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُۥ وَمَا كَسَبَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayḍāwī calls the passage a report of the unseen whose fulfillment matched what happened.
rows.anchor: فهو إخبار عن الغيب طابقه وقوعه
